title: Is there anything out there?

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: What we are trying to do is not look at the past, the reports, trying to figure out, because they were anecdotal, the data was incomplete. What I've seen publicly is always fuzzy and unclear. Instead, the sky is not classified, so we will take our own data. And once we have several tens of these observatories in many locations, we will get all this of magnitude more data than was ever reported in the past, and it will be of high quality because...

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: have full control over the instruments and we understand, we calibrate them. And then we use machine learning and artificial intelligence to analyze that data and figure out whether we are looking at a natural object like a bird

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: we are looking at a human-made object like a balloon

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: extraterrestrial. That would be the main question. Is there anything out there? It's obviously a mixed bag. You have all kinds of objects, but

turns.speaker: Guest Speaker 1
turns.text: question is whether any of them could be extraterrestrial.
